title: Radio and signals
summary: Licence-free and common radio channels in Canada and the US, with what licence each needs, plus phonetic alphabet, Morse code, distress words and ground-to-air signals. Use it to call for help by radio, or without one.

steps.text: Find your radio's service in the first table and read the licence column for your country.

In an emergency use the right channel: any FRS or GMRS channel, CB 9, or marine 16. On a boat, aircraft or vehicle in immediate danger say Mayday three times; on foot say “Emergency, emergency, emergency”. Then who, where, what is wrong and how many people.
steps.warn: Only call Mayday for real, immediate danger. A false distress call is an offence in Canada and the US.

steps.text: No radio, or no answer? Signal in threes with whistle, mirror or fire, and lay out a ground-to-air symbol.

notes:
## Licence-free and common channels

| Service | Channels, power | Canada | US |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FRS** | 22 channels. Ch 1–7 and 15–22 (462.55–462.725 MHz): 2 W ERP. Ch 8–14 (467.5625–467.7125 MHz): 0.5 W | No licence (ISED RSS-210) | No licence (FCC) |
| **GMRS** | Shares all 22 FRS channels (8–14 limited to 0.5 W). US adds 467 MHz repeater channels and up to 50 W on main channels. Canada: the same 22 channels at 2 W ERP, nothing extra | No licence (ISED) | FCC licence, age 18+; covers immediate family (FCC) |
| **MURS** | 151.820, 151.880, 151.940, 154.570, 154.600 MHz; 2 W; no repeaters | Not in ISED's licence-exempt standard; do not assume it is legal | No licence (FCC) |
| **CB** | 40 channels, 26.965–27.405 MHz; 4 W AM/FM, 12 W SSB; no add-on amplifiers | No licence (ISED RIC-18) | No licence (FCC) |
| **Marine VHF** | Ch 16 = 156.800 MHz: distress, safety, calling | Operator on a Canadian vessel needs a ROC-M certificate (TC) | Recreational boat in US waters: no licence or permit. Foreign trips need more (FCC) |
| **Amateur** | 146.520 MHz (2 m) and 446.000 MHz (70 cm): national FM calling frequencies (ARRL, RAC) | Basic Qualification certificate (RAC) | FCC amateur licence (FCC) |
| **Weather (receive only)** | 162.400, .425, .450, .475, .500, .525, .550 MHz | Weatheradio Canada ended 16 Mar 2026; Coast Guard marine broadcast continues (ECCC) | NOAA Weather Radio, all seven (NWS) |

- **CB ch 9** (27.065 MHz): emergencies and traveller help only (FCC, ISED). **Ch 19** (27.185 MHz): road information in many areas. In Canada ch 11 is a calling channel; ch 13 and 23 are used for rescue (ISED RIC-18).
- Any GMRS channel may carry an emergency call, and emergency traffic has priority on every channel (FCC).
- A false distress call is an offence in both countries (FCC, ISED).
- US GMRS rules keep the word "Mayday" for a ship, aircraft or vehicle in immediate danger. Use plain words ("emergency") otherwise (FCC).
- Do not modify certified radios (ISED).

## Phonetic alphabet and Morse

Words are the ICAO spelling words (FAA, ISED RIC-18). Morse is the ITU code. Dash = 3 dots. Gap inside a letter = 1 dot, between letters = 3, between words = 7 (ITU).

| Letter | Say | Morse | Letter | Say | Morse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Alfa | `.-` | N | November | `-.` |
| B | Bravo | `-...` | O | Oscar | `---` |
| C | Charlie | `-.-.` | P | Papa | `.--.` |
| D | Delta | `-..` | Q | Quebec | `--.-` |
| E | Echo | `.` | R | Romeo | `.-.` |
| F | Foxtrot | `..-.` | S | Sierra | `...` |
| G | Golf | `--.` | T | Tango | `-` |
| H | Hotel | `....` | U | Uniform | `..-` |
| I | India | `..` | V | Victor | `...-` |
| J | Juliett | `.---` | W | Whiskey | `.--` |
| K | Kilo | `-.-` | X | X-ray | `-..-` |
| L | Lima | `.-..` | Y | Yankee | `-.--` |
| M | Mike | `--` | Z | Zulu | `--..` |

Digits (FAA, ITU): 1 One `.----`, 2 Two `..---`, 3 Tree `...--`, 4 Four `....-`, 5 Fife `.....`, 6 Six `-....`, 7 Seven `--...`, 8 Eight `---..`, 9 Niner `----.`, 0 Zero `-----`.

**SOS** is `... --- ...` sent as one group, with no gaps (USCG 33 CFR 87).

## Distress words

- **Mayday** (said three times): grave and imminent danger, immediate help needed. Call: MAYDAY x3, THIS IS, your name x3, position, nature of the distress, help wanted, number of people. Speak slowly. Repeat until answered (FCC).
- **Pan-Pan** (three times): very urgent message about the safety of a vessel, aircraft, vehicle or person. Ranks below Mayday (FCC).
- **Sécurité** (three times): navigation or weather warning (FCC).
- Use ch 16 (156.800 MHz) at sea. 121.5 MHz is an aircraft distress frequency (FCC, TC AIM).

## No radio: signals

- **Three of anything** is a distress call: whistle blasts, mirror flashes, fires, rock piles. Repeat every 1–2 minutes (Utah, AdventureSmart).
- **Whistle**: three blasts. It carries farther than a voice (Utah).
- **Mirror**: sight through a V of two fingers, flash in threes. Do not flash at aircraft unless it is a survival situation (Utah).
- **Fire**: smoke by day (add green leaves). Three fires in a triangle at night (TC AIM, Utah). Lights, strobes and camera flashes also work at night (TC AIM).
- **Arms**: slowly raise and lower both arms, outstretched (USCG 33 CFR 87).

**Ground-to-air symbols** (TC AIM). Make them at least 2.4 m (8 ft) long, in strong contrast, from fabric, wood or stones.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| V | Need assistance |
| X | Need medical help |
| N | No |
| Y | Yes |
| Arrow | Going this way |

Canada-only extras: LL all is well, F food and water, L fuel and oil, W need repairs.
